changelog/CHANGELOG.html.title: Changelog | Android Wireless Pairing
changelog/CHANGELOG.html.summary: Changelog [1.0.2] - 2026-10-09 Added When the running adb server is too old to send device name, API and ADB Wi-Fi version, a "Restart adb Server" button appears at the bottom (after confirmation, stops the server and starts it again with the newest installed adb) If another program starts an older server again after the restart, the window says so Fixed The previous adb server kept running after installing Platform-Tools (on macOS the server stayed alive on the replaced files): the server is now restarted with the new adb when the install finishes [1.0.1] - 2026-10-09 Changed Platform-Tools install confirmation is shown as an in-window popup instead of an OS dialog (install location, administrator permission note, license link) Fixed Windows: Platform-Tools install Stops the adb server before installing and doesn't restart it during the install (the running adb.exe was locked and couldn't be replaced) Runs sdkmanager with administrator permission (UAC) when Unity's SDK folder isn't writable (Program Files) Wraps sdkmanager.bat in paths with spaces with cmd /s /c On cancel or timeout, also stops sdkmanager's child java process Windows sdkmanager didn't read the "y" answer from stdin, so nothing was installed without license acceptance: after you agree, the acceptance is written to licenses/android-sdk-license before running On failure, shows the actual error message instead of a progress line Corrected the requirement for device name and API to Platform-Tools 37 or newer (a 36.0.0 server doesn't support host:track-mdns-services) Starting the adb server: waits at most 1 second for output after exit so it doesn't hang while the server daemon holds the output pipe. Treated as success if the server is running even when the exit code reports failure [1.0.0] - 2026-10-09 Changed Rebuilt the window to follow Android Studio's "Pair devices over Wi-Fi" flow (one UXML per view) Lists devices with wireless debugging turned on, live (name · ADB Wi-Fi version · IP:port · API) Pair → per-device screen: QR tab (default) / pairing code tab Pairing code is a 6-box input on a dimmed overlay. Boxes advance automatically; pasting fills and submits Connection success screen Device info comes from the adb server socket's host:track-mdns-services stream (no polling; text fallback for older servers) Pairing and connecting also go through the server socket (host:pair, host:connect) instead of the adb CLI, reducing server restarts caused by adb version mismatches Starts the server itself only when it doesn't respond for 6+ seconds, using the newest installed adb Added ADB Wi-Fi version circle: v1.0 gray · v2.0 green (for Android 17) Themes: Android Studio / Unity (Dark / Light follows the editor skin), theme selection screen on first launch Languages: English / 한국어 Change theme and language from the ⋮ menu at the top right or Preferences > Android Wireless (saved per user in EditorPrefs) Install banner when Platform-Tools is below 37 (installs with Unity SDK's sdkmanager after license agreement) Notice screen when the Android Build Support module is missing IBM Plex Sans KR font (Bold is a subset of used glyphs, AW Sans KR) EditMode tests for protobuf parsing Removed adb path field, direct connect, connected devices section, log (adb path override moved to Preferences) [0.1.0] - 2026-10-06 Added Initial release: wireless debugging pairing editor window with QR / pairing code

manual/connect-device.html.title: Connect a Device | Android Wireless Pairing
manual/connect-device.html.summary: Connect a Device Pair and connect an Android 11+ device over Wi-Fi. Once paired, the device reconnects whenever you turn on wireless debugging. 1. Prepare the device Connect your computer and the device to the same Wi-Fi network. Enable Developer options on the device. Turn on Settings > Developer options > Wireless debugging. When asked whether to allow wireless debugging on this network, tap Allow. 2. Open the window In Unity, select Tools > Android Wireless Pairing. The first time, a theme selection screen appears. See Settings. 3. Device list Devices with wireless debugging turned on appear in the list automatically. No refresh needed. Column Description Name Device name ADB Wi-Fi ADB Wi-Fi version the device supports. v1.0 is a gray circle, v2.0 is green. IP Address & Port The device's wireless debugging address API Android API level Devices that are already connected show Connected instead of the Pair button. Type a device name or IP in the search field to filter the list. Note Device name, API, and ADB Wi-Fi version require Platform-Tools 37 or newer. See Requirements. 4. Pair using QR code Click Pair next to the device. A QR code appears on the Pair using QR code tab. On the device, tap Developer options > Wireless debugging > Pair device with QR code and scan the code. Pairing and connecting happen automatically. A success screen appears when done. 5. Pair using pairing code Use this when you can't scan the QR code. Click Pair next to the device and select the Pair using pairing code tab. On the device, tap Developer options > Wireless debugging > Pair device with pairing code. The device shows a 6-digit Wi-Fi pairing code. The device appears under Available Wi-Fi devices in the window as Available to pair. Click Pair and enter the 6-digit code shown on the device. Each box moves to the next one as you type. Paste the code into any box (Ctrl/Cmd+V) to fill all boxes and submit at once. A success screen appears when pairing and connecting are done. Click Pair another device on the success screen to return to the list. Unpair a device On the device, open Developer options > Wireless debugging > Paired devices, select your computer, and tap Forget. To unpair all computers at once, tap Developer options > Revoke USB debugging authorizations.

manual/index.html.title: Android Wireless Pairing | Android Wireless Pairing
manual/index.html.summary: Android Wireless Pairing Android Wireless Pairing is an editor window that pairs and connects Android 11+ devices over wireless debugging from inside the Unity Editor. It follows the same flow as Pair devices over Wi-Fi in Android Studio, so you can deploy builds to a device without a USB cable. Features Lists devices with wireless debugging turned on, live, on the same network. Pairs by scanning a QR code or entering a 6-digit pairing code, then connects automatically. Shows each device's ADB Wi-Fi version (v1.0 / v2.0). Installs the latest Platform-Tools from the window when yours are out of date. Two themes (Android Studio / Unity) and two languages (English / 한국어). Check the Requirements, then follow Installation and Connect a Device.

manual/installation.html.title: Installation | Android Wireless Pairing
manual/installation.html.summary: Installation Install the package Install Android Wireless Pairing from its Git repository URL in the Unity Package Manager. Make sure Git is installed. Open the Package Manager. Click the + button and select Install package from git URL.... Enter the repository URL and click Install. https://github.com/NK-Studio/com.nkstudio.android-wireless.git Install with manifest.json You can also add it directly to dependencies in Packages/manifest.json. "com.nkstudio.android-wireless": "https://github.com/NK-Studio/com.nkstudio.android-wireless.git"

manual/requirements.html.title: Requirements | Android Wireless Pairing
manual/requirements.html.summary: Requirements Unity Unity 6000.0 or newer The Android Build Support module The window finds and pairs devices with the adb in Unity's Android module. Without the module, the window only shows a notice that it can't be used. Add Android Build Support to your editor version in Unity Hub. This is an editor-only package and adds no runtime code to your builds. Device and network A device running Android 11 or newer Your computer and the device must be on the same Wi-Fi network. Android SDK Platform-Tools What the window shows depends on the Platform-Tools version in Unity's Android SDK. Platform-Tools Available Below 37 Device list, pairing, connecting (no device name, API, or ADB Wi-Fi version) 37 or newer Device name, API, and ADB Wi-Fi version; ADB Wi-Fi 2.0 (Android 17+ devices) If Platform-Tools is below 37, you can update it from the window. See Settings > Update Platform-Tools.

manual/settings.html.title: Settings | Android Wireless Pairing
manual/settings.html.summary: Settings All settings are saved per user (EditorPrefs), not per project. Each team member can use different settings without affecting the project. Theme and language The first time you open the window, a theme selection screen appears. Choose Android Studio or Unity and click Continue. Dark / Light follows the Unity Editor skin. You can change these anytime from the ⋮ menu at the top right of the window. Menu Description Theme Android Studio / Unity Language English / 한국어 Theme Setup… Opens the theme selection screen again. Preferences… Opens Preferences > Android Wireless. Preferences Change the following in Edit > Preferences > Android Wireless (macOS: Unity > Settings > Android Wireless). Setting Description Theme Window theme Language Window language adb Path Override Used only to start the adb server when it isn't running. Leave empty to pick the newest installed adb automatically. Show Theme Setup Next Time Click this button to show the theme selection screen the next time you open the window. Update Platform-Tools If Platform-Tools in Unity's Android SDK is below 37, an update notice appears above the device list. Click Install. Review the Android SDK License Agreement notice and click Agree and Install. The latest Platform-Tools is installed with the sdkmanager included in Unity's SDK. Click Later to skip for now.

manual/troubleshooting.html.title: Troubleshooting | Android Wireless Pairing
manual/troubleshooting.html.summary: Troubleshooting Device doesn't appear in the list Make sure your computer and the device are on the same Wi-Fi network. Guest networks or networks that block device-to-device traffic may prevent discovery. Make sure Wireless debugging is on. It can turn off when the device locks or changes networks. Make sure the device runs Android 11 or newer. See Requirements. Device name or API shows "—" If the serial number appears in place of the device name and ADB Wi-Fi and API show "—", the adb server that's currently running is an older version. Check the note at the bottom of the window and fix it based on the cause. An update notice for Platform-Tools also appears Platform-Tools in Unity's Android SDK is below 37. Install the latest version with Update Platform-Tools. The adb server is restarted with the new version when the install finishes. Only "The running adb server is an older version" appears Unity's adb is up to date, but another program (scrcpy, Homebrew adb, an older Android Studio SDK, etc.) started the server first with an older adb. Click Restart adb Server at the bottom and confirm with Restart. The server is stopped and started again with the newest installed adb. Other tools using adb, such as Android Studio or Logcat, briefly lose their connection. Running adb kill-server in a terminal does the same. The window starts the server again with the newest adb shortly after. If "Another program started an older adb server again" appears after restarting, that program keeps relaunching the server. Find out which adb it is, then update that program or point it at the same Android SDK. macOS: lsof -nP -iTCP:5037 -sTCP:LISTEN Use the PID from the output to find the executable path. ps -p <PID> -o comm= Windows (Command Prompt): netstat -ano | findstr :5037 Find the PID in the last column on the Details tab of Task Manager, then right-click > Open file location. "Can't reach the adb server" The window connects to the running adb server (127.0.0.1:5037 by default) to find devices. If the server doesn't respond, it starts one with the newest installed adb. If it still can't connect, click Open Preferences… and set the adb path yourself. Make sure a firewall or security software isn't blocking adb. List briefly empties or the connection drops This can happen when Unity and another tool (such as Android Studio) keep stopping and restarting each other's adb server. If Preferences > External Tools > Kill external ADB instances is on, Unity stops adb servers that aren't from its own SDK. Turn it off if you use other tools at the same time. If Unity's SDK and the other tool use different Platform-Tools versions, they restart each other's server. Update Unity's SDK, or point Preferences > External Tools > Android SDK at the same SDK. "Android Build Support isn't installed" Add the Android Build Support module to your editor version in Unity Hub, then restart the editor. Other issues See Troubleshoot wireless connection in the Android documentation.
